reason: Section 136 is a coherent court power for directly affected persons or residents challenging or confirming local instruments, with a repeat-application refusal rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court orders quashing or declaring by-laws, resolutions, or orders

evidenceText: quash it in whole or in part for illegality

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify who may apply, the Court's power to quash for illegality or declare force and effect, and when the Court may refuse a repeat application raising substantially the same matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may seek court review of a by-law, resolution, or order and what quashing, declaration, or repeat-application powers the Court has.

reason: Section 137 is a substantive prohibition provision listing the main compliance failures and obstruction prohibited under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibited non-compliance with by-laws, regulations, terms, orders, Board decisions, and duties
proposedGroups.reason: The section prohibits violating or failing to comply with by-laws, regulations, imposed terms or conditions, orders or demands, Board decisions, and obstructing a person performing duties under the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the categories of non-compliance and obstruction prohibited by section 137.

reason: Section 138 separates offence/category consequences from prosecution limits and appeal-related time extension.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offences, offence categories, and continued prosecution after conviction
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections make listed Schedule A violations offences, tie them to Provincial Offences Procedure Act categories, and state that conviction does not bar further prosecution for continued neglect or failure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how offences are created and categorized under section 138 and why conviction does not bar further prosecution for continued non-compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Six-month prosecution limit and Board appeal extension

evidenceText: shall not be commenced after six months

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set a six-month limit from discovery of the offence and extend that period by the time between notice of appeal and final disposition when a Board appeal is made.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prosecution limitation period and how a Board appeal extends it.

reason: Section 139 is a focused rule identifying who may commence offence proceedings under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Names in which offence proceedings are commenced

evidenceText: shall be commenced in the name of the Minister

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that proceedings are commenced in the name of the Minister, the local government clerk, or another council-designated person.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall whose name may be used to commence offence proceedings under the Act.

reason: Section 140 is a substantive enforcement bridge for rural plan by-laws in rural districts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister enforcement of rural district rural plan by-laws

evidenceText: authorized to enforce a rural plan by-law

proposedGroups.reason: The section authorizes the Minister to enforce a rural plan by-law in a rural district and applies sections 132 to 139 with necessary modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may enforce rural district rural plan by-laws and that enforcement provisions apply with modifications.

reason: Section 141 defines the former Act for the transitional Part.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Meaning of former Act for transitional provisions
proposedGroups.reason: The section defines former Act as the Community Planning Act, chapter C-12 of the Revised Statutes, 1973, for the purposes of the Part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which statute is meant by former Act in the transitional Part.

reason: Section 142 is a transitional continuity rule for municipal development plans under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former municipal development plans deemed municipal plans

evidenceText: shall be deemed to be a municipal plan

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems former municipal development plans in force before commencement to be municipal plans under the Act, valid and continuing until amended or repealed to the extent consistent with the Act or a statement of provincial interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how municipal development plans under the former Act continue as municipal plans under the Act.

reason: Section 143 is a transitional continuity rule for resolutions made under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former Act resolutions deemed made under the Act

evidenceText: shall be deemed to have been made under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems specified former Act resolutions in force before commencement to have been made under the Act and to continue until amended or repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former Act resolutions continue under the Act.

reason: Section 144 is a transitional continuity rule for by-laws made under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former Act by-laws deemed made under the Act

evidenceText: shall be deemed to have been made under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems former Act by-laws in force before commencement to have been made under the Act and to continue until amended or repealed to the extent consistent with the Act or a statement of provincial interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former Act by-laws continue under the Act and what consistency limits apply.

reason: Section 145 is a transitional continuity rule for permits, approvals, and orders under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former permits, approvals, and orders deemed made under the Act
proposedGroups.reason: The section deems permits, approvals, and orders in force before commencement to have been made under the Act and to continue until amended or repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former Act permits, approvals, and orders continue under the Act.

reason: Section 146 is a transitional continuity rule for agreements and contracts entered under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former agreements and contracts continued under the Act
proposedGroups.reason: The section continues former Act agreements and contracts in force before commencement as if made under the Act, subject to provisions of the Act that affect them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former Act agreements and contracts continue and remain subject to the Act.

reason: Section 147 is a transitional processing rule for applications received before the section came into force.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Pre-commencement applications dealt with under existing process
proposedGroups.reason: The section requires applications received before commencement to be dealt with under the process in effect in the municipality, rural community, or village when received.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which process applies to applications received before the section came into force.

reason: Section 148 is a transitional appeal-processing rule for appeals commenced before the Board before commencement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Pre-commencement Board appeals dealt with under the Act
proposedGroups.reason: The section requires appeals commenced under the previous Act before the Assessment and Planning Appeal Board before commencement to be dealt with under the process in effect under the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how appeals already before the Board before commencement are processed.

reason: Section 149 is a transitional continuity rule for planning advisory committee members appointed under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former planning advisory committee members deemed appointed under the Act

evidenceText: shall be deemed to have been appointed

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems former Act planning advisory committee members to have been appointed under subsection 5(2) and to continue until resignation, reappointment, or replacement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former planning advisory committee members continue in office under the Act.

reason: Section 150 is a transitional continuity rule for payments still due or owing under section 45 of the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former Act section 45 payments continue despite repeal

evidenceText: payments are still due or owing

proposedGroups.reason: The section continues section 45 of the former Act as if not repealed for payments still due or owing for specified facility costs or cost shares.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when section 45 of the former Act continues for unpaid facility-related amounts.

reason: Section 151 is a transitional continuity rule for the person holding the Provincial Planning Director office under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Provincial Planning Director deemed appointed under the Act

evidenceText: shall be deemed to have been appointed the Provincial Planning Director

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems the person holding the former Provincial Planning Director office to have been appointed under section 9 and to continue until resignation, reappointment, or replacement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Provincial Planning Director continues in office under the Act.

reason: Section 152 is a transitional continuity rule for municipal and rural community planning directors and officers appointed under the former Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former planning directors and planning officers deemed appointed under the Act

evidenceText: shall be deemed to have been appointed as a planning director or planning officer

proposedGroups.reason: The section deems former municipal and rural community planning directors and officers to have been appointed as planning directors or planning officers under section 10 and to continue until resignation, reappointment, or replacement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how former planning directors and officers continue in office under the Act.

reason: The target only repeals the former Community Planning Act and does not provide a continuing study topic beyond the repeal itself.
